events.narrative: The recorded polity authorized a long-duration collective undertaking; offices committed labor and resources to its declared goal.
Decades of labor levies, workshop quotas and specialist appointments concentrated resources; dissent and displaced workplaces were entered in the public record.
Engineers surveyed a physically attainable launch route and documented propulsion tests.
A long-duration Ark Project committed the polity to carrying registered people and records beyond the planet.
Selection registers recorded the actual baseline-human candidate population. The selection rule was contested; no unrecorded hereditary lineage was inferred.
A registered launch complex and vessel were constructed over decades.
A registered launch attempt proceeded. The observation records whether liftoff occurred, without asserting a successful departure.
Identified Observer-era orbital hardware physically denied the registered exodus attempt through launch destruction. Activation, purpose and rule remain unknown.
Identified Observer-era orbital hardware physically denied the registered exodus attempt through guidance capture. Activation, purpose and rule remain unknown.
Identified Observer-era orbital hardware physically denied the registered exodus attempt through propulsion suppression. Activation, purpose and rule remain unknown.
Identified Observer-era orbital hardware physically denied the registered exodus attempt through orbital containment. Activation, purpose and rule remain unknown.
Identified Observer-era orbital hardware physically denied the registered exodus attempt through silent denial. Activation, purpose and rule remain unknown.
The attempted exodus failed; launch registers, a memorial and surviving vessel or wreck observations record the loss. Why orbital hardware denied it remains unknown.
Tracking lost the departing vessel beyond local coverage. Local departure succeeded; destination and survival are unknown.
Survey teams mapped a new depth interval using registered drilling and support equipment.
A Deep Descent Project committed successive generations of work to deeper exploration.
Permanent shafts, ventilation and transit structures were completed.
Multiple registered expeditions used the shaft; roster and depth logs survive.
Survey records show a substructure outside prior maps; its content and maker were not classified.
The final registered expedition reached unprecedented depth before communications became irregular.
Surface rosters document an attempted evacuation after communications failed; only a small fraction returned.
The Last Descent left missing expedition members and an inaccessible shaft. What they found, what killed them and whether any system acted intentionally remain unknown.
The expedition returned with mapped strata and reusable engineering records; no catastrophe was recorded.
Astronomical records identify a long-term receiving direction and measured equipment requirements.
Officials disputed the survey, cost and meaning of possible signals; these arguments did not establish any signal origin.
The polity authorized the Far-Sky Array, a Deep-Space Listening Array built across decades.
Specialist workshops completed a large receiving array and its records service.
The array began recorded observations of the selected sky region.
Long observation found no meaningful signal. The spending inquiry removed the sponsoring offices and the facility was abandoned.
Repeated narrowband signals were measured. Their origin and meaning remain unknown.
Array activation and an identified orbital-system state change were close in time. This is a recorded temporal correlation; causality remains unknown.
Operators repeatedly interpreted one measured pattern for decades. Records establish fixation, not a message or its mechanism.
Later instrumentation shows that the array transmitted. Who changed it and why remain unknown.
The array remains active, tracking the same recorded sky region; no purpose or signal origin has been established.
